prose: A widely shared primer uses an escape room to explain reinforcement learning environments, a theme the author says was everywhere at this year's ICML. The mapping: the room is the environment with its objects, rules and feedback; the flashlight, box and keypad are the tools; escaping is the task; and the binary escaped-or-not result after an hour is the verifier. Swap the human for an AI agent and you have an RL environment - a clean way to see why verifiable, well-instrumented tasks have become the bottleneck and the currency of post-training.
highlights: Escape-room analogy for RL environments: environment, tools, task, verifier
RL environments were a central theme at this year's ICML
Binary escape-or-not outcome illustrates what a clean verifier looks like
Frames verifiable tasks as the bottleneck of post-training
